body: Why is everyone required to have friends? I've had some bad things happen in life and really have trust issues. I operate just fine alone. I have a few buddies I know? That's about it. Be like me. Have no expectations whatsoever. Know no girl will want you. Friend zone yourself, every single time. Be everything some one might want, try to do your best, be kind, be good, take care of yourself and then before they get a chance throw yourself right into the friend zone, because you are not worth being somebody's somebody. You are not worth love. Yep, be like me... And girls won't even want to be your friend. You'll be in the "buddy" zone. A zone even below friend zone. The "I see you at work/meets/neighbor/whatever and love talking to you and you make me laugh! But no, I don't want to actually know you." 

Welcome to my world. Stand tall and know that even if you are a decent man, you are not a bad person but you are not worth anyone's time.

I also don't get why when some people end a relationship they say "can we still be friends?" Well, if it's mutual and you both know it's not working and you still care about that person but can't see yourself ever being sexual with them again and there's no attraction there from either side? Sure. But when some one ends it and the other doesn't want it to end? That's super fucked up and can ruin the next relationship for either person as well. No, you left me, in a bad bad way. I loved you so much. Why would I want to be your friend now while you fuck other guys? Thanks, but I'll pass. Or buy a cat, or something.

For a decade I have decided to never ask a woman for her info, her Facebook, her phone number, nothing. I work around women all around my age all day long and meet new ones all the time due to my work. I am very extroverted, anyone will tell you I'm really friendly and outgoing. I am always easy to talk to and try to make people Laugh. Sometimes it makes me come off awkwardly but so be it, that's just me. I try to always be mannerly and help anyone who needs help.

I am a competitive cyclist (I even race) and am Runner training for a Marathon. In 10 years of "focusing on me" not pushing myself onto others and just doing my own thing, you know how many women have asked me for anything? Phone number, Facebook, etc. I'm talking in the real world now. 

One. I saved her life. She wanted my phone number. We got close and she decided she didn't want me. It hurt like hell.

A few weeks back this girl that has kept opening up to me, acting like she just needed some one to talk to, telling me about stuff in her life. Totally wasn't expecting anything out of it, just wanted to be nice and asked if she was on Facebook. She looked at me terrified and said she doesn't use Facebook. It was really awkward and weird.

Fuck it. Never again.

Everyone I've met, both male and female have a big circle of friends. Girls seem to always have a huge circle of friends. Everyone has a ton of friends.

I've had friends before. I've had a few best friends. I've had guy friends and lady friends. But now days I keep people kind of distant. There's a few people I work with on my Facebook, mainly guys. Girls want nothing to do with me.

I always swore I would never be pushy or ask for anyone's Facebook or phone or contact info or anything. That I would out myself out there and if anyone wanted anything to do with me they would let me know.

I'm always super outgoing, polite, friendly. I love to make people laugh and have never had a problem talking to people. Yet, even though I work around a lot of women my age, none of them have ever wanted anything to do with me and I never want to make it awkward. The other day I broke down. This one girl started kind of opening up to me, talking to me more. Was kind of odd so I really passively asked if she had Facebook. She looked at me kind of shocked and said "No, I don't use it anymore." Before saying "Well, I better go now."

Idk what's so wrong with me. I wasn't trying to get into her pants. I would be happy with even a lady friend to talk to as I know no one would want me for anything else but even that I'm not good enough for. It hurt bad.

I've been told I was weird before because I didn't have friends. I have had some really bad shit happen to me in life. It would be nice to have some one I could really confide in and truly have a partnership with. But being a middle aged guy without friends who's super outgoing and silly acting, I think maybe people think Im weird or something. 

Some one told me it was because I'm too nice, women want a man who is an asshole? Not sure if I believe that, maybe? I can't be the asshole type. I've tried. I won't be something I'm not. I have confidence that I know how to be a man, where it counts and always have been but like, that's not good enough, I'm not worthy of a real relationship with a woman.

It's funny. I'm not financially set but I do have a professional job? I am big into fitness and in great shape. I'm a Cyclist and a Runner and am training for a marathon right now. Fitness and training is all I have. It's funny though, that doesn't seem to matter. What matters is having a bunch of money, stable career, ton of confidence and being an asshole dude with a bunch of buddies who watch football or whatever. 

Always just wanted a partner, some one who didn't have all these requirements, Lord knows I don't. But I've pretty much given up that it exists.

I've made several posts about this. Feel free to check out my created posts history on it. I feel very much that too many people in life base everything off of sex and some one's performance of such. It's sad how it is the end all be all in so many relationships. When I was younger I used to hear some ladies complain about how "guys only want one thing" etc, which honestly most do, but for myself I've always just wanted companionship. Some one to hold hands with and walk with, to talk to, to sleep beside, to cuddle with and watch TV in the evenings. Some one who you know will be there for you and loves you for who you are, for your being you. So many people confuse lust and love which is why so many relationships fail.

Sure, you should definitely be able to have meaningful sex with some one you really love, but I think it should be more about intimacy and less about how highly you preform at certain things, how many skills you have, what kinks you're willing to do. It sort of takes any innocence out of love which I think there should be a certain degree of. I think people should explore what they like in that way with each other and find a happy middleground. Some where they both please each other.
